newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE DESPITE CASH SHORTAGE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE DESPITE CASH SHORTAGE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market held largely stable at their previous levels on Thursday despite tight liquidity, dealers said.
"The market was short by about Z$62.9 million (at Wednesday's close) probably due to treasury bills taken up yesterday, and there's nothing much maturing today," one dealer said.
He said the central Reserve Bank had not indicated any intention of coming into the market with a special tender, which it has been doing since Monday as a way of mopping up excess liquidity.
But dealers said the central authority would hold the usual Thursday weekly treasury bill auction, one of its tools for raising money for the government.

On Thursday morning, discount houses were selling treasury bills in the market at 17.50 percent, unchanged from Wednesday, and bankers acceptances also held steady at 18.15 and 17.85 percent (buying and selling respectively).
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were at 18.75 percent (buying) and 18.35 percent (selling) while call money ranged from 17.75 to 18 percent.
